 Key Points
 Hotels and aviation made up 37 of 59 tracked capital moves in October, with hotel deals driven by debt paydown, receivership, and insolvency while buyers consolidated portfolios.
 Aviation capital went toward future capacity and the debt to fund it: Avolon ordered 250 aircraft, Aviation Capital Group 75, and Southwest, IndiGo, and Allegiant arranged financing.
 Venture funding stayed modest — 10 of 17 rounds were $5 million or less — and AI dollars went into plumbing such as agent-to-inventory connections, guest messaging automation, and post-booking price tracking.
 Summary
 Skift tracked 59 capital moves across travel in October 2026, and hotels and aviation accounted for 37 of them — but the money moved for different reasons. Hotel capital largely changed hands: Pandox sold seven Nordic hotels to pay down debt, receivers sold two Shimao hotels in Hong Kong, two Indian hotels transferred through insolvency, and buyers consolidated portfolios, including Endeavor's seven hotels around Chicago Midway Airport and Sunday PropTech's deal for Fletcher's roughly 170 hotels. Aviation capital went into future capacity and the debt behind it, with Avolon ordering 250 aircraft, Aviation Capital Group ordering 75, and Southwest, IndiGo, and Allegiant lining up financing. Startup funding stayed small — 10 of 17 venture financings were $5 million or less — and the AI money that moved went into infrastructure: connecting AI agents to travel inventory, automating hotel guest messaging, and tracking hotel prices after booking. Booking Holdings' plan to invest up to $100 million in its own AI trip-management startup, Vayo, is contingent on product progress. Consolidation continued in travel technology, with SITA agreeing to two airline and airport technology acquisitions in under two weeks and Duetto buying FLYR's hotel revenue management business.
